sources.title: Al-Baladhuri: Conquests of Sind, translated in Elliot and Dowson, History of India, volume 1
sources.note: Direct primary translation read, printed pp.113-130, especially pp.119-123: Muhammad ibn Qasim, Dahir’s death, negotiated submissions, tribute and temples. Ninth-century author, not an eyewitness; nineteenth-century translation and editorial claims treated cautiously. The collection’s Chachnama extract dates Dahir’s death to 712, printed p.172; no exact day or inflated casualty totals adopted. All passages from this collection counted together.

sources.title: Derryl N. MacLean: Chachnama, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct article read, paragraphs on the pre-Islamic dynasties, indigenous Aror tradition, caste and romantic/mythic material. The article accepts a lost Arabic precursor, while Ahmed’s newer interpretation challenges this; the disagreement is preserved. No exact Chach accession date derived from this source.

sources.title: Manan Ahmed: The long thirteenth century of the Chachnama
sources.note: Direct official Sage abstract read: 1226 Uch, multi-genre political text, challenge to simple translation model. Full-text printed p.465 checked through exact indexed scholarly repository query: site:citeseerx.ist.psu.edu "The long thirteenth century" "465" "scribe". That page supplies the scribe/queen/succession storyline and legitimacy/advice themes. Repository https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=15642eb0f27139c0070312c01358dac8fa5dad2c&repid=rep1&type=pdf failed direct extraction; no claim full paper was directly read.

sources.title: Xuanzang: Country of Sin-tu, Buddhist Records of the Western World, translated by Samuel Beal
sources.note: Direct primary translation read, Book XI chapter15 opening: wheat/millet, livestock and single-humped camels, colored medicinal salts. Only these observations used; religious stereotypes, mass family counts and miraculous stories excluded. Combined with the Chinese witness and 137 words already attributed to the same original work in maitraka-kingdom, despite its different translation/URL.

sources.title: Xuanzang: Great Tang Record of the Western Regions, CBETA Chinese edition, volume 11
sources.note: University-hosted CBETA PDF exact indexed text checked: site:ss.ncu.edu.tw/~calin/scripture/t51/T51n2087.pdf "信度國" "宜穀稼" resolves to web.ss.ncu.edu.tw. Printed PDF p.104, Taisho T51 no.2087 p.937a, opening 信度國周七千餘里. Direct fetch returned502. Chinese name checked against Beal’s Sindh section; modern pinyin and type explicitly identified as modern presentation. This is an external Chinese witness, not local Sindhi writing.

sources.title: CRAST archaeological mission: Banbhore, 2014-2015 fieldwork
sources.note: Direct mission report read: location on Gharo creek, identification debate, pre-Islamic and Islamic craft materials, 2015 building and water tank provisionally linked to ninth-century changes. The water tank is explicitly later than Dahir. No 4000-fragment total assigned to the pre-conquest period. Conservatively combined with the related 2016 report abstract as one project-report work.

sources.title: Felici, Fusaro and colleagues: Archaeological excavations at Banbhore, 2016 preliminary report
sources.note: Direct institutional abstract read, Parthica18 pp.125-173: long occupation at least second to early thirteenth century, transitional phases, honeycomb moulds linked to smelting/coinage. Abstract only; full PDF is restricted to repository administrators and was not read. Combined conservatively with CRAST’s related project summary.

sources.title: Government of Sindh: Archaeological Museum Banbhore, Thatta
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue outline read: painted pre-Muslim pottery up to seventh century, eighth-century storage jars and white-paste pottery, ninth-to-twelfth-century Chinese pottery. Only specified dated categories used; typographic errors in headings not reproduced.

sources.title: Alexander Fishman: A hoard of unpublished silver coins from the Baluchistan/Sind border, Journal of the Oriental Numismatic Society201 (2009)
sources.note: Original society PDF downloaded directly and extracted in cache ons.pdf/ons.txt; printed pp.13-16. Public small-money example: p.14 sample254, most1.15-1.25g, average16mm, XRF silver about85%; provenance is dealer-reported and date/issuer tentative. Writing p.15 type3A HaMaVa; p.14 meaning explicitly unresolved. No exact ruler or excavated provenance claimed; period632-712 is only approximate dynastic context.

sources.title: N. G. Majumdar: Explorations in Sind, Memoirs of the Archaeological Survey of India48 (1934)
sources.note: Original printed p.21, Tharro, Buddhist Remains, checked through exact indexed primary query: site:tamildigitallibrary.in "Explorations" "offertory" "Tharro". Direct PDF returned404. Text reports over100 unbaked clay tablets from a circular mound, Buddha/chaitya types, Buddhist creed in North Indian characters dated seventh/eighth centuries. The preceding prehistoric flints and unrelated stone chambers are not assigned to the tablets’ era. No unverified full Sanskrit creed quoted.

proposedOverrides.name: Kingdom of Sind and the Arab conquest
proposedOverrides.summary: Dahir’s pre-conquest Sind kingdom; the imported interval also includes the Arab provincial period after 712.

batchIdentityNotes.decoded: world-700 Polygon bounds60.5904E23.8195N72.8629E30.9351N. Broad Indus/Sindh and neighboring Makran/Baluchistan/frontier areas; not a certified Dahir border. Some western areas already under caliphal rule before700.
batchIdentityNotes.historicalScope: Late pre-conquest kingdom and Arab transition, with seventh-century and later material explicitly dated. Approximate Chach-family context circa630-711; defeat712; no dynasty survival to800 inferred.
batchIdentityNotes.related: sindh900-1000 and sind1492-1500 are different phases; Rajput networks are not a substitute for Sind. Existing Umayyad card remains the conquering imperial context, not an alias. No successor navigation added without separately validated geometry.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Chachnama is thirteenth-century Persian and its relationship to lost earlier narratives is disputed. Banbhore/Debal identification remains debated. Ninth-century tank and continuing port are later context. Reported border silver hoard has uncertain provenance, issuing authority, meaning and possibly function. Chinese sample is external, not local Sindhi.
